UnitStatement: The semantic-matrix-build skill is consumed by TASK and its brief must make task scope, semantic scope, status policy, and expected outputs explicit.
A semantic-matrix-build brief must set TaskSkill to semantic-matrix-build.
ScopePath must be an absolute path to exactly one deliverable or production unit folder.
ScopePath is the TASK local scope for semantic-matrix-build.
Tasks must request generation of _SEMANTIC.md for one scope.
ExpectedOutputs must include _SEMANTIC.md and the TASK run record.
Required semantic fields should be placed in RuntimeOverrides unless local TASK convention passes them top-level.
deliverable_folder must be an absolute path to the same folder as ScopePath.
decomposition_path must be an absolute path to the decomposition document and is used only for traceability.
DECOMP_VARIANT must be PROJECT, SOFTWARE, or DOMAIN.
STATUS_POLICY must be PRESERVE_CURRENT, ADVANCE_ON_PASS, or NO_STATUS_TOUCH.
The default STATUS_POLICY for ORCHESTRATOR Phase 2.3 is PRESERVE_CURRENT.
Normal ORCHESTRATOR Phase 2.3 uses ScopePath as the TASK run and context anchor.
Normal ORCHESTRATOR Phase 2.3 provides RuntimeOverrides.deliverable_folder as the skill-local deliverable anchor.
semantic-matrix-build must create or overwrite _SEMANTIC.md.
A normal ORCHESTRATOR Phase 2.3 brief must set ApplyEdits true and authorize _SEMANTIC.md as writable.
A brief for status advancement on PASS is used only when project policy makes semantic-matrix-build own SEMANTIC_READY advancement.
A status-advancement brief must authorize _STATUS.md as a writable target.
On audit PASS under status advancement policy, semantic-matrix-build sets or verifies SEMANTIC_READY and appends History.
On audit FAIL under status advancement policy, _STATUS.md state remains unchanged.
PROJECT variant reads Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
SOFTWARE variant reads the same document set and terminology as PROJECT.
DOMAIN variant reads all non-metadata markdown files not prefixed with underscore, typically Scoping.md and KA files.
A format-sensitive run generates exactly one _SEMANTIC.md for exactly one deliverable folder.
A format-sensitive run keeps the lens deliverable-conditioned but not deliverable-literal.
Final matrix cells must be category-level phrases of two to five words.
Step 2 projections must resolve semantic phrases rather than restating formulas.
Matrix Summary must use compact markdown tables rather than bullet lists.
Matrix Z must be inserted before Matrix Summary.
Validator PASS must not be claimed unless the repo validator actually ran.
Multi-deliverable scope is not accepted for semantic-matrix-build.
Cross-deliverable scanning or comparison is not accepted for semantic-matrix-build.
ORCHESTRATOR authoring _SEMANTIC.md inline instead of dispatching TASK is not accepted.
Missing decomposition_path is not accepted.
Missing STATUS_POLICY in an ORCHESTRATOR Phase 2.3 brief is not accepted.
A semantic-matrix-build brief that asks the skill to edit production documents is not accepted.
A brief that combines STATUS_POLICY=ADVANCE_ON_PASS with omitted _STATUS.md write authorization is not accepted.
A valid semantic-matrix-build run requires ScopePath to exist and be a directory.
A valid semantic-matrix-build run requires deliverable_folder to exist, be a directory, and resolve to ScopePath.
A valid semantic-matrix-build run requires _CONTEXT.md to exist in deliverable_folder.
A valid semantic-matrix-build run requires decomposition_path to be provided.
If the decomposition_path file cannot be read, the run records that fact and does not invent decomposition content.
A valid semantic-matrix-build run writes _SEMANTIC.md to deliverable_folder.
Production documents are read-only during semantic-matrix-build.
No sibling deliverable folder is scanned during semantic-matrix-build.
No files outside the effective bounded task brief write authorization are written.
All eight derived matrices must appear in sequence as C, F, D, K, G, X, T, and E.
Canonical matrices A and B are reproduced exactly and not re-derived.
Interpreted matrices C, F, D, X, and E include intermediate collections and all three interpretation steps for every cell.
Matrix Summary appears after Matrix Z and contains compact markdown tables for C, F, D, K, G, X, T, and E.
STATUS_POLICY is honored exactly.
The repo validator is run when available and permitted.
The _SEMANTIC.md header includes generated date, variant, perspective, framework, audit status, phase or status ruling, and Inputs Read.
Inputs Read lists metadata and production documents as read, not present, or absent.
SourceRefs use a path plus a best-effort heading anchor when possible.
The required matrix order is A, B, C, F, D, K, G, X, T, E, Matrix Z, then Matrix Summary.
Every matrix section has a Result table.
Summary sections use markdown tables rather than bullets.
Matrix Z appears between Matrix E and Matrix Summary and is not counted as a semantic matrix.
Required dimensions are C 3x4, F 3x4, D 3x4, K 4x3, G 3x4, X 4x4, T 4x4, and E 4x4.
Matrix C construction must show L_C(i,j) as the sum over A(i,k) times B(k,j), then C(i,j) as I(row_i, col_j, L_C(i,j)).
Matrix F construction must show L_F(i,j) as the sum over C(i,k) times B(k,j), then F(i,j) as I(row_i, col_j, L_F(i,j)).
Matrix D construction must show L_D(i,j) as A(i,j) plus resolution times F(i,j), then D(i,j) as I(row_i, col_j, L_D(i,j)).
Matrix K construction must show K(i,j) equals D(j,i).
Matrix G construction removes the wisdom row from Matrix B.
Matrix X construction must show L_X(i,j) as the sum over K(i,k) times G(k,j), then X(i,j) as I(row_i, col_j, L_X(i,j)).
Matrix T construction must show T(i,j) equals B(j,i).
Matrix E construction must show L_E(i,j) as the sum over X(i,k) times T(k,j), then E(i,j) as I(row_i, col_j, L_E(i,j)).
Every interpreted cell must contain every contributor product required by its formula.
Step 1 must explicitly show r times c equals a resolved anchor phrase.
Step 1 anchor phrases must be semantic rather than restating the row-column coordinate frame.
Step 2 must explicitly show every p_n equals a times t_n.
Every Step 2 projection must end with a resolved semantic phrase.
Every contributor in L must have exactly one Step 2 projection.
Step 3 must state that the centroid selects a final phrase or equivalent.
Step 3 must select only one final phrase.
Interpretation work must not jump directly from Step 1 to Step 3.
Semantic products must use the asterisk operator rather than x or prose-only joins.
Final cells in Result tables and Matrix Summary must be populated.
Final cells in Result tables and Matrix Summary must be exactly one semantic unit, not a list.
Final cells must be two to five words except canonical inherited B, G, and T values.
Final cells should prefer two to three words when meaning remains complete.
Final cells must not contain algebra leaks such as intersection or summation symbols.
Final cells must not contain an unresolved plus operator between semantic terms.
Final cells must not exceed about 80 characters.
Final cell values must not literally contain the row or column labels for that cell.
Final cells must not contain exact code clauses, event-name lists, file paths, implementation paths, numeric requirements, equipment tags, or other instances.
Final cells must not contain engineering correctness claims, recommendations, fitness judgments, or acceptance rulings.
The semantic lens must be relevant to the deliverable without becoming a requirements summary.
A valid perspective mentions known source-state caveats at a category level without particulars.
Audit scans final cell values in every Result and Summary table for C, F, D, K, G, X, T, and E.
On audit FAIL, the run is marked FAIL.
On audit FAIL, semantic-matrix-build does not repair, regenerate, or re-audit within the same run.
On audit FAIL, semantic-matrix-build does not advance status.
If _SEMANTIC.md is written during an audit FAIL run, its header shows Audit: FAIL.
On audit FAIL, the run report lists matrix, cell, value, and reason.
On audit PASS, _SEMANTIC.md is marked Audit: PASS.
On audit PASS, STATUS_POLICY is applied exactly.
On audit PASS, the repo validator is run when available and permitted.
PRESERVE_CURRENT leaves lifecycle state unchanged and reports preservation by runtime policy.
ADVANCE_ON_PASS sets or verifies SEMANTIC_READY only when _STATUS.md editing is authorized, and leaves state unchanged on FAIL.
NO_STATUS_TOUCH prohibits all _STATUS.md edits.
Status regression is never allowed.
_CONTEXT.md is not modified by semantic-matrix-build.
_REFERENCES.md is not modified by semantic-matrix-build.
_DEPENDENCIES.md is not modified by semantic-matrix-build.
MEMORY.md is not modified by semantic-matrix-build.
_STATUS.md is modified only when status policy and TASK authorization allow it.
_SEMANTIC.md is created or overwritten only inside deliverable_folder.
A missing or non-directory deliverable_folder is reported as FAILED_INPUTS.
A missing _CONTEXT.md is reported as FAILED_INPUTS.
An omitted decomposition_path is reported as FAILED_INPUTS.
A ScopePath and deliverable_folder disagreement is reported as FAILED_INPUTS.
A missing production document is recorded absent and the run continues.
A missing _REFERENCES.md is recorded as not present and the run continues.
A missing MEMORY.md is recorded as not present and the run continues.
Audit failure is reported as FAIL with matrix, cell, and reason.
An unavailable validator is reported as unavailable.
A clean run reports RUN_STATUS=SUCCESS or the local TASK success token.
A clean run reports deliverable identity, DECOMP_VARIANT, _SEMANTIC.md path, audit result, validator result, status action, production document safety, write-scope safety, and failing-cell absence.
semantic-matrix-build generates _SEMANTIC.md as a deliverable-local semantic lens for one production unit.
The semantic lens is deliverable-conditioned because _CONTEXT.md and production documents shape vocabulary and perspective.
The semantic lens is not deliverable-literal because matrix cells are semantic categories, types, behaviors, and values rather than restated requirements or implementation details.
Each semantic-matrix-build run starts from canonical Matrix A and Matrix B.
semantic-matrix-build derives exactly C, F, D, K, G, X, T, and E in order.
The only primary output of semantic-matrix-build is deliverable_folder/_SEMANTIC.md.
semantic-matrix-build runs in TASK generic shell mode with ScopePath set to the deliverable folder.
The skill may narrow runtime behavior but must not widen the effective bounded task brief write authorization.
When TASK and the skill disagree about write authorization or tool use, the narrower instruction wins.
A run report must surface contradictions between TASK and skill authorization.
Instruction conflicts must be reported rather than silently reconciled.
If DECOMP_VARIANT is absent, semantic-matrix-build defaults it to PROJECT and reports that default.
If ADVANCE_ON_PASS requests _STATUS.md editing without authorization, semantic-matrix-build does not edit status.
semantic-matrix-build reads only inside deliverable_folder except for the decomposition document used for traceability.
semantic-matrix-build reads _CONTEXT.md, _STATUS.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, MEMORY.md, and production documents in that order when present.
Missing production documents are recorded as absent and do not fail the run.
semantic-matrix-build must not read sibling deliverable folders.
semantic-matrix-build may write only inside deliverable_folder.
semantic-matrix-build may overwrite _SEMANTIC.md as its primary output.
semantic-matrix-build may write _STATUS.md only if STATUS_POLICY requires it and TASK authorizes it.
semantic-matrix-build never modifies production documents or deliverable metadata files other than authorized _STATUS.md.
_SEMANTIC.md includes a one to three sentence Perspective near the top.
The Perspective names what the deliverable is for at a semantic level.
The Perspective identifies the kinds of knowledge the lens must carry.
The Perspective includes relevant source-state caveats at a category level when present.
The Perspective avoids engineering correctness claims.
The Perspective avoids exact code clauses, event-name lists, file paths, line numbers, implementation paths, and other particulars.
Final matrix cells must be deliverable-conditioned.
Final matrix cells must be category-level rather than requirement-level.
Final matrix cells must be one phrase only.
Final matrix cells must be two to five words.
Final matrix cells must be free of row and column axis labels.
Final matrix cells must be free of algebra symbols, unresolved plus signs, and raw formula text.
Semantic multiplication combines two semantic units into their intersection.
Semantic addition groups terms into a collection.
Semantic addition must not leak into final cell values.
Every list-valued cell must be interpreted into one atomic semantic unit.
Every interpreted cell must show exactly three interpretation steps.
Step 1 computes and resolves the axis product a = r times c.
Step 2 computes and resolves every contributor projection.
Step 3 selects one final cell phrase.
The Step 3 final phrase captures the shared semantic core of all resolved projections.
Matrix A canonical values must be used exactly and not edited.
Matrix A normative-guiding cell is prescriptive direction.
Matrix A normative-applying cell is mandatory practice.
Matrix A normative-judging cell is compliance determination.
Matrix A normative-reviewing cell is regulatory audit.
Matrix A operative-guiding cell is procedural direction.
Matrix A operative-applying cell is practical execution.
Matrix A operative-judging cell is performance assessment.
Matrix A operative-reviewing cell is process audit.
Matrix A evaluative-guiding cell is value orientation.
Matrix A evaluative-applying cell is merit application.
Matrix A evaluative-judging cell is worth determination.
Matrix A evaluative-reviewing cell is quality appraisal.
Matrix B canonical values must be used exactly and not edited.
Matrix B data-necessity cell is essential fact.
Matrix B data-sufficiency cell is adequate evidence.
Matrix B data-completeness cell is comprehensive record.
Matrix B data-consistency cell is reliable measurement.
Matrix B information-necessity cell is essential signal.
Matrix B information-sufficiency cell is adequate context.
Matrix B information-completeness cell is comprehensive account.
Matrix B information-consistency cell is coherent message.
Matrix B knowledge-necessity cell is fundamental understanding.
Matrix B knowledge-sufficiency cell is competent expertise.
Matrix B knowledge-completeness cell is thorough mastery.
Matrix B knowledge-consistency cell is coherent understanding.
Matrix B wisdom-necessity cell is essential discernment.
Matrix B wisdom-sufficiency cell is adequate judgment.
Matrix B wisdom-completeness cell is holistic insight.
Matrix B wisdom-consistency cell is principled reasoning.
Matrix C uses L_C(i,j) as the sum over A(i,k) times B(k,j).
Matrix C uses C(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_C(i,j)).
Matrix F uses L_F(i,j) as the sum over C(i,k) times B(k,j).
Matrix F uses F(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_F(i,j)).
Matrix D uses L_D(i,j) = A(i,j) plus resolution times F(i,j).
Matrix D uses D(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_D(i,j)).
Matrix D uses exactly two contributors: the A cell and the resolution-transformed F cell.
Matrix K is the transpose of D with K(i,j) = D(j,i).
Matrix G is created by removing the wisdom row from Matrix B.
Matrix X uses L_X(i,j) as the sum over K(i,k) times G(k,j).
Matrix X uses X(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_X(i,j)).
Matrix T is the transpose of B with T(i,j) = B(j,i).
Matrix E uses L_E(i,j) as the sum over X(i,k) times T(k,j).
Matrix E uses E(i,j) = I(row_i, col_j, L_E(i,j)).
_SEMANTIC.md must be written in the prescribed order.
Matrix Z is a delimiter that prevents summary tables from being parsed as Matrix E result work.
Matrix Z is not a semantic matrix.
Inputs Read SourceRefs use path anchors, not present, absent, or location TBD forms.
An input must not be claimed as read unless it was actually read.
Before reporting success, semantic-matrix-build audits every Result table and every Matrix Summary table.
If audit fails after writing _SEMANTIC.md, the file header is marked Audit: FAIL.
If audit fails, semantic-matrix-build does not repair and re-audit in the same run.
With PRESERVE_CURRENT, semantic-matrix-build does not change lifecycle state and records preservation by runtime policy.
With ADVANCE_ON_PASS, semantic-matrix-build sets or verifies SEMANTIC_READY only when _STATUS.md editing is authorized.
With NO_STATUS_TOUCH, semantic-matrix-build does not edit _STATUS.md.

The TASK run report includes run status, deliverable identity, resolved folder, variant, semantic path, audit result, status action, validator result, missing inputs, failing cells, and production document safety.
When the validator exists and tool use is permitted, semantic-matrix-build runs tools/validation/validate_semantic_matrix.py on deliverable_folder.
If the validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build reports validator not available and does not claim validator PASS.
When invoked for DOMAIN, semantic-matrix-build reads Knowledge Type non-metadata markdown documents and uses DOMAIN terminology while keeping the matrix algebra unchanged.
semantic-matrix-build tool posture is reasoning-first.
Deterministic tools are used only for validation and filesystem safety when available.
The preferred tool sequence starts by reading files inside ScopePath needed by the skill.
The preferred tool sequence generates _SEMANTIC.md by reasoning from the skill contract.
The preferred tool sequence runs the semantic audit specified in QA_CHECKS.md.
validate_semantic_matrix.py is required in normal repo runs when available and permitted.
validate_semantic_pipeline_scope.py is required when project ORCHESTRATOR policy calls for it and the tool is available.
If a validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build reports unavailable and does not claim validator PASS.
Reasoning is required for deriving the deliverable perspective.
Reasoning is required for choosing deliverable-conditioned but non-literal semantic phrases.
Reasoning is required for resolving each axis anchor.
Reasoning is required for resolving every projected contributor in Step 2.
Reasoning is required for selecting centroid attractors.
Reasoning is required for auditing final cells for semantic product validity.
Tools or scripts must not be used to bypass semantic reasoning work.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim cross-deliverable conclusions.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim engineering correctness.
semantic-matrix-build must not claim validator PASS unless the validator actually ran.
The normal write target for semantic-matrix-build is deliverable_folder/_SEMANTIC.md.
_STATUS.md is a conditional write target only when status policy requires it and TASK authorization allows it.
When the validator is unavailable, semantic-matrix-build completes semantic audit manually and reports validator unavailable.
When _CONTEXT.md is missing, semantic-matrix-build fails with FAILED_INPUTS.
When a production document is missing, semantic-matrix-build records absent and continues.
When a status edit is requested but unauthorized, semantic-matrix-build does not edit _STATUS.md and reports the contradiction.
When tool output contradicts file content, semantic-matrix-build reports the discrepancy and does not hide it.
When a brief asks for out-of-scope writes, semantic-matrix-build refuses those writes and reports a scope violation.
